content:
I've spent a week with the iPhone 18 Pro, after using an iPhone Air for a full year. While both phones have their strengths, my main takeaway about the iPhone 18 Pro is this: it's completely uncompromising. Here's what I mean by that.

iPhone 18 Pro: The best camera system, battery life, and performance

If you're looking to buy a new iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro is almost certainly an incredibly strong choice.

I've had my iPhone 18 Pro for a week now—the burgundy colorway—and it's replaced my iPhone Air. I loved the Air, but it's hard to match the zero-compromises standard Apple has set with the iPhone 18 Pro.

  • Compared to the Air, the iPhone 18 Pro's cameras are better and offer more versatility. The telephoto and ultrawide lenses suit specific shooting scenarios, but even the main lens on the iPhone 18 Pro is superior.
  • Battery life is equally impressive. I previously felt the iPhone Air's battery was enough to get through a day, with an occasional top-up around midday. But after using the iPhone 18 Pro, I don't even have to think about the battery level anymore.
  • Performance is also outstanding. The A20 Pro chip makes everything on the iPhone fast and smooth, and I've noticed Siri AI feels more responsive. With the added vapor chamber, I've yet to experience overheating—something the Air would occasionally do.

I'm not a professional photographer, and if you're looking for battery tests or performance benchmarks, my colleague Chance's iPhone 18 Pro review has everything you need. But after a week with the iPhone 18 Pro, the word "best" has been floating around in my head.

The iPhone 18 Pro (and Pro Max) feature Apple's most advanced camera system ever, the best battery life, and performance that's stronger than any other model. I've also noticed some subtle improvements: better built-in speaker quality and improvements to the Dynamic Island are highlights.

All of the above are measurable differences, but what I'm most relieved about is being able to rest easy knowing my iPhone delivers Apple's best performance where it matters most. No more wondering: when taking photos of family, would another iPhone do a better job? Will the system slow down again?

Setting aside all the merits of the iPhone 18 Pro, I'll admit I'm still very intrigued by the upcoming iPhone Duo.

iPhone Duo shares some tradeoffs with the iPhone Air, but is equally hard to resist

The iPhone Air and iPhone Duo share a lot in common. Beyond similar design language, both also have their fair share of shortcomings.

Just like my iPhone Air, the iPhone Duo's camera system will be inferior to the iPhone 18 Pro's. Battery life will likely be similar to the Air, but certainly not as good as the Pro Max, and I'd expect sustained performance to be slightly worse. Additionally, the iPhone Duo will lack Face ID and the Action button.

However, despite these tradeoffs, I'm still very much looking forward to trying this phone out for myself.

Because it brings a lot of attractive innovations the iPhone 18 Pro doesn't have. The foldable design is arguably one of the biggest hardware changes in iPhone history.

I'm thoroughly enjoying my time with the iPhone 18 Pro right now. But guess what? A few days ago, when I picked up my iPhone Air, here's what happened.

I couldn't help but exclaim: "Wow."

After a year with the Air's slimness, I'd taken it for granted. But after a few days with the iPhone 18 Pro, I rediscovered that futuristic feel of the Air. I'd expect the iPhone Duo to deliver a similar feeling—not just in design, but in practicality.

I'm very excited about the prospect of putting an iPad-like experience in my pocket. Although I do feel somewhat conflicted about the drawbacks the Duo will bring, it doesn't diminish the anticipation.

The era when Apple offered only one "best" iPhone is over. If you want a phone with absolutely no compromises, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max seem exceptional. But if you're looking for something more futuristic and unique, I can't wait to try the iPhone Duo.

What are your thoughts on choosing between the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
